The petition will be lodged with Charles, Jamaica’s head of state, on Monday.

Local authorities blamed the attack – which took place late on Friday – on the rebel National Liberation Army (ELN).

A host of financial institutions said they were due to receive billions of yuan in capital from state institutions including the ministry of finance and even the company that runs the country’s tobacco monopoly.

euronews.title: Mediterranean Sea now at spa temperature, daily average 28.54°C on 13 August
euronews.description: On 13 August the Mediterranean averaged 28.54°C, its highest level since comparable records began in 1940, Aemet reports, capping a summer with the warmest July on record at sea and in mainland Spain.

euronews.description: Speaking at the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Davos this year, von der Leyen said the EU was working on a "massive European investment surge" in Greenland in a bid to ramp up Arctic security.

euronews.description: The Puerto Rican artist has picked up seven Emmy Awards for his Super Bowl LX show at the pre-gala, ahead of the main ceremony on 14 September in Los Angeles.

euronews.description: AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund casts his ballot in Saxony-Anhalt, where his party is seeking a historic breakthrough in the state election.

euronews.description: Netanyahu defended Israel’s 2025 strike on Doha and called Qatar a “hostile state," while Qatar separately accused Iran of selectively quoting a Qatari security assessment to justify attacks on its territory.

euronews.title: Germany's satellite rocket marks first successful launch from continental Europe
euronews.description: German company Isar Aerospace has placed its Spectrum rocket in low Earth orbit at the second attempt, becoming the first European firm to do so with its own launcher and hitting the first milestone of ESA's European Launcher Challenge.

euronews.title: Berlin planning 'protective shield' to defend against sabotage, report says
euronews.description: The new plan would see the creation of a "Cyberdome," a network of digital sensors that would help seek out and intercept hacking attempts, Bild reported.

euronews.title: Chainsaw maker STIHL chief calls for longer hours without extra pay
euronews.description: In an opinion piece for Euronews, Dr Nikolas Stihl, chairman of world-leading chainsaw maker STIHL, calls for reforms including a 40-hour working week without extra pay to safeguard Germany's prosperity and welfare state.

euronews.title: Iran claims strike on US navy drone, US says it's "total lie" as Hormuz clashes rage on
euronews.description: As the US-Iran clashes in Hormuz intensify, Iran claimed it struck an unmanned US navy vessel on Sunday, which the US denied as a "total lie". Iran has ramped up its offensive military response in Hormuz warning against any new US attacks.

euronews.title: Polls open in Saxony-Anhalt as AfD predicted to win state election
euronews.description: A large AfD victory would pile more pressure onto Merz and his increasingly unpopular coalition. The party has been polling at more than 40%.

euronews.description: Mount Anak Krakatoa is an active volcano that sits in the Sunda Strait, between the islands of Java and Sumatra.

euronews.description: Yuri Ushakov, a Kremlin aide, called US talks with Putin "extremely frank" and said that the US side had "put forward a number of ideas on possible routes to a settlement."

euronews.title: Exhibition celebrates legacy of 80-year-old Hungarian painter Sándor Pinczehelyi in Pécs
euronews.description: The exhibition showcasing the work of Hungarian painter Sándor Pinczehelyi in Pécs is open to visitors until 8 November 2026 at the M21 Gallery in the Zsolnay Cultural Quarter.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, élections régionales en Allemagne : l’AfD effectue une poussée historique en Saxe-Anhalt mais les conséquences restent incertaines
lemonde.description: Largement en tête dans cette région, Alternative pour l’Allemagne, menée par Ulrich Siegmund, pourrait devenir le premier parti d’extrême droite à diriger un Land depuis 1945, à condition qu’il obtienne la majorité absolue ou tisse des alliances à l’issue du dépouillement. La CDU s’effondre et le sort du chancelier Friedrich Merz est en débat.

lemonde.title: Loïk Le Priol face à la justice pour l’assassinat de l’ex-rugbyman Federico Martin Aramburu
lemonde.description: Le procès de l’ancien commando de marine et de son ami Romain Bouvier s’ouvre lundi à Paris. Le 19 mars 2022, les deux militants d’extrême droite ont tiré sur l’ancien international argentin à la suite d’une bagarre alcoolisée, boulevard Saint-Germain, à Paris.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les premières discussions avec Volodymyr Zelensky ont été « très significatives », a déclaré Steve Witkoff, en visite à Kiev avec Jared Kushner
lemonde.description: Une session de pourparlers impliquant les deux envoyés américains, la délégation ukrainienne et des responsables européens pour la sécurité nationale se tient dimanche soir dans la capitale ukrainienne.

lemonde.title: En lançant sa fusée en orbite, la start-up bavaroise Isar Aerospace bouleverse l’écosystème spatial européen
lemonde.description: La fusée Spectrum a placé sur orbite cinq satellites samedi. Un succès qui permet à l’entreprise allemande de prétendre jouer un rôle de complément à Ariane-6 face à l’américain SpaceX.

lemonde.title: Fabien Roussel officialise sa candidature à la présidentielle et promet « un projet de rupture »
lemonde.description: Après un vote favorable des militants du PCF à 72 %, le communiste a confirmé sa candidature à l’Elysée au JT de TF1, assurant avoir fait « un choix largement réfléchi » malgré la multiplication des candidatures à gauche.

lemonde.title: Mary Austin, la discrète gardienne du temple de Freddie Mercury
lemonde.description: Elle a été la compagne, puis l’assistante personnelle, et, enfin, l’héritière du flamboyant leader du groupe Queen. A 75 ans, Mary Austin dévoile dans un premier livre des archives inédites de Freddie Mercury, qui la qualifia d’“amour de sa vie” jusqu’à sa mort.

lemonde.title: Incendie en vallée d’Aspe, dans les Pyrénées-Atlantiques : 125 hectares brûlés, « la météo n’est toujours pas favorable et des points chauds persistent »
lemonde.description: L’incendie de végétation qui embrase depuis mercredi les hauteurs de la vallée d’Aspe (Pyrénées-Atlantiques) concerne désormais 125 hectares, contre 105 hectares samedi, a-t-on appris dimanche soir auprès de la préfecture, qui évoque une situation « plutôt stable »

lemonde.title: Canicule : six départements du sud et du sud-est en vigilance orange lundi, selon Météo France
lemonde.description: Ardèche, Aude, Drôme, Gard, Hérault et Vaucluse resteront à l’orange dimanche et lundi, précise le prévisionniste, qui a enregistré ce week-end des températures inédites pour un mois de septembre dans plusieurs localités.

lemonde.title: Guerre au Soudan : des preuves supplémentaires de l’existence d’un programme d’armes chimiques en 2024
lemonde.description: Le « Washington Post » et le « New York Times » ont eu accès à des notes internes, des vidéos, des photos et des interceptions téléphoniques attestant que des bombes au chlore ont été développées par l’armée soudanaise et utilisées pendant au moins six mois contre leurs adversaires paramilitaires.

lemonde.title: « Une grosse dernière fête » : dans les coulisses du Z Event 2026, ultime édition du marathon caritatif sur Twitch
lemonde.description: Cocréé par le streameur ZeratoR, l’événement est devenu en dix ans l’un des rendez-vous majeurs de l’Internet français, inspirant de nombreuses initiatives similaires. Pour ce dernier numéro, quelque 330 créateurs de contenu se sont rassemblés ce week-end dans une ambiance survoltée.

lemonde.title: Luz, dessinateur : « Après l’attentat de 2015, j’ai été habité par des fantômes »
lemonde.description: « Je ne serais pas arrivé là si… » Chaque semaine, « Le Monde » interroge une personnalité sur un moment décisif de son existence. Le dessinateur rescapé de l’attentat contre « Charlie Hebdo » évoque notamment sa rencontre décisive avec Cabu.

lemonde.title: Kimi Antonelli, auteur d’une remontée spectaculaire, remporte un Grand Prix d’Italie de F1 qui a viré au fiasco pour Ferrari
lemonde.description: Le prodige de Mercedes, parti du fond de la grille, s’est imposé dimanche, devenant le premier Italien à triompher à Monza depuis 60 ans. Dans les rangs de la Scuderia, Lewis Hamilton, qui n’a pu faire mieux que sixième, voit ses rêves de sacre s’éloigner.

lemonde.title: Comment le poisson-éléphant filtre les impulsions électriques pour reconnaître ses proies
lemonde.description: Une équipe américaine a analysé les connexions neuronales de l’animal pour comprendre son mode si particulier de perception du monde.

lemonde.title: Au festival Visa pour l’image, l’Iranien Hashem Shakeri témoigne d’un peuple « coupé du monde »
lemonde.description: Le photographe, qui expose son travail à Perpignan, est l’un des rares à avoir pu témoigner des répercussions de la guerre sur le quotidien des habitants de son pays.

lemonde.title: Dans une Libye divisée, Donald Trump mise sur son « art du deal » pour se poser en faiseur de paix
lemonde.description: Après quinze ans de discrétion sur le dossier libyen, Washington veut réconcilier les autorités rivales de l’Est et de l’Ouest autour d’un accord de partage du pouvoir négocié entre quelques seigneurs locaux. Loin d’apaiser le pays, cette initiative déclenche une fébrile recomposition des rapports de force et met à nu la fragilité des alliances de part et d’autre.

lemonde.title: Yémen : 141 morts depuis samedi dans les affrontements entre rebelles houthistes et forces gouvernementales
lemonde.description: Ce bilan porte à plus de 300 le nombre de morts depuis l’offensive lancée jeudi par les houthistes et visant à garder le contrôle de l’accès à la mer Rouge.

rfi.title: 'We are family', says EU chief Ursula von der Leyen at start of Greenland visit
rfi.description: European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen arrived in Greenland on Sunday for a two-day visit aimed at reaffirming the bloc's support for the Arctic island coveted by the US President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: Germany’s far-right AfD eyes historic breakthrough in Saxony-Anhalt election
rfi.description: Voters in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt head to the polls on Sunday in an election that could hand the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) its biggest political breakthrough yet.

rfi.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner arrive in Kyiv after talks with Putin in Russia
rfi.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday for talks with the Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky a day after meeting the Russian president Vladimir Putin to discuss proposals over how to end the four-year war between Russia and Ukraine.

rfi.title: France's school uniform experiment unravels with only mixed results
rfi.description: Two years after France began trialling uniforms in schools, the experiment is sputtering to a close after failing to convince pupils or teachers.

rfi.title: Driven from their island, Zambian fishermen pay price of Chinese expansion
rfi.description: Hundreds of fishermen say they were violently driven from an island in southern Zambia and have been unable to return to their fishing grounds for more than three years, after a Chinese-owned fishing company expanded its operations in the area. They say they lost their homes and livelihoods, have never received compensation and are still seeking justice. An RFI investigation has traced what happened to the community and the Chinese company's growing presence on Lake Kariba.

rfi.title: Turkey seeks Black Sea shipping deal as attacks threaten grain trade
rfi.description: Turkey is racing to restore safe passage for cargo ships in the Black Sea as attacks on shipping disrupt grain exports and push up prices. Russia and Ukraine are major global wheat exporters, but Black Sea trade has been severely disrupted as both sides step up attacks on shipping and port infrastructure.

rfi.title: UN backs effort to drop Mercator map and show size of Africa more accurately
rfi.description: The United Nations voted on Saturday for a shift away from the 16th-century Mercator global map towards one more accurately reflecting the true size of countries.

rfi.title: A nation trapped: photographing the broken promises of Sudan's revolution
rfi.description: Syrian-born photographer Abdulmonam Eassa travelled to Sudan as the fall of its longtime dictator, toppled by massive protests, raised hopes of a democratic rebirth. Instead, he witnessed the country descend into another military takeover, rivalry and all-out war. RFI spoke to him about the resulting photo series, War in Sudan: A Nation Trapped, which is now on show at the Visa pour l'Image festival in southern France.

rfi.title: French tennis player Gea hails surge into second week at US Open
rfi.description: Unseeded Frenchman Arthur Gea declared himself physcially fit and ready to fight on Monday night for a first appearance in the quarter-finals at a Grand Slam tournament.

rfi.title: Paris 'Dragon Ball' theme park in doubt as Japanese owners deny granting licence
rfi.description: The Japanese rights holders for the Dragon Ball anime franchise have denied giving permission for a theme park in the Paris region based on the popular series. The confusion follows French President Emmanuel Macron's announcement of a deal with Saudi Arabia to build three parks outside the capital.

rfi.title: Algerian football chiefs name Hemdani to replace Petkovic as head coach
rfi.description: The Algerian Football Federation (FAF) confirmed on Sunday the appointment of the former Marseille and Glasgow Rangers midfielder Brahim Hemdani as head coach.

rfi.title: PSG boss Enrique plays down slow start to Ligue 1 campaign after Monaco defeat
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain head coach Luis Enrique on Saturday played down his side's faltering start to the 2026/2027 Ligue 1 season following a 2-1 home defeat to Monaco.

rfi.title: How China’s Paracel expansion extends its military reach towards Vietnam
rfi.description: China is rapidly expanding two artificial islands in the disputed Paracel Islands, with analysts saying the new facilities could strengthen Beijing’s military reach towards Vietnam and along key South China Sea shipping routes.

rfi.title: DRC eyes Jerusalem embassy as Tshisekedi seeks Israel's support
rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo plans to move its embassy in Israel from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem following talks between President Félix Tshisekedi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in a rare diplomatic step that could also strengthen Kinshasa's ties with Washington and its access to military support.

rfi.title: France unveils €1.1bn emergency aid for farmers after record heat
rfi.description: ​France has announced €1.1 billion in emergency aid for farmers after record heat and drought caused severe damage to crops, pastures and water supplies.

rfi.title: How France and Britain’s far right are building a populist ‘entente cordiale’
rfi.description: Jordan Bardella will address Reform UK's party conference in Birmingham on Friday, putting the French far-right leader alongside Nigel Farage as both men seek to strengthen their political profiles. The appearance also marks closer ties between two of Europe's most successful populist radical-right parties that share similar positions on immigration but have not always been natural allies.

rfi.title: Paris families sue mayor over alleged child abuse in after-school care
rfi.description: Around 15 families who allege their children suffered violence and sexual abuse in Paris after-school care have filed a complaint against the city and its Socialist mayor, Emmanuel Grégoire, as well as his predecessor Anne Hidalgo.

rfi.title: Tunisia court upholds long sentences in mass trial of opposition figures
rfi.description: Tunisia's top court has turned down the final appeal of dozens of opposition leaders, lawyers and businessmen convicted in a major conspiracy case, in a ruling opponents said further entrenches President Kais Saied's authoritarian rule.

france24fr.title: La nette victoire de l’AfD en Saxe-Anhalt menace "le système politique allemand"
france24fr.description: L’AfD est arrivée largement en tête lors de l’élection dans la Land de Saxe-Anhalt, dimanche. Son candidat, Ulrich Siegmund, est aux portes du pouvoir, mais l’AfD semble avoir raté de peu la majorité absolue espérée pour former un gouvernement sans avoir à trouver d’alliés. Si l’AfD surmonte ce dernier obstacle, ce serait un tremblement de terre politique sans précédent en Allemagne qui pourrait coûter cher au chancelier Friedrich Merz.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Fabien Roussel officialise sa candidature avec le PCF
france24fr.description: Le secrétaire national du Parti communiste français (PCF), Fabien Roussel, a officialisé dimanche sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle française de 2027 au JT de TF1.

Festival de Deauville : votre film américain préféré ?
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis se classent deuxièmes pour le nombre de films produits avec 500 à 700 films par an ! Alors, le Festival du Cinéma Américain de Deauville a pour but de mettre en avant le meilleur de tout ce qui se fait outre-Atlantique. Mais de l'autre côté de l'écran, les spectateurs ont aussi leur mot à dire. Quel est votre film américain préféré ? Notre journaliste Gaëlle Fonseca est allée à votre rencontre sur les planches de Deauville pour vous poser la question.

france24fr.title: Sauvetages au Népal, frappes russes sur Kiev, un match de kokpar : la semaine en images
france24fr.description: Retour sur les temps forts de l'actualité de la semaine et les images les plus marquantes : les opérations de secours au Népal après une crue meurtrière, les nouvelles frappes nocturnes massives sur Kiev ou encore un match de kokpar aux World Nomad Games organisés au Kirghizstan.

france24fr.title: Allemagne en direct : victoire "historique" de l'extrême droite en Saxe-Anhalt mais pas de majorité absolue (estimations)
france24fr.description: L’AfD est arrivé largement en tête des élections régionales en Saxe-Anhalt avec plus de 44% des voix, selon les estimations de la ZDF et de l'ARD. Le parti d’extrême droite allemand obtiente une victoire qu'il qualifie d'historique. Il obtiendrait 39 sièges au parlement régional, tout proche de la majorité absolue de 42 sièges. Suivez en direct les résultats du scrutin et les réactions sur France 24.

france24fr.title: Arsenal et Chelsea se retrouvent pour un derby londonien déjà déterminant
france24fr.description: Dimanche soir, Arsenal accueille Chelsea pour reprendre la tête du championnat en cas de victoire. Mikel Arteta et Xabi Alonso, amis depuis l'enfance, s'affronteront pour la première fois en tant qu'entraîneurs de Premier League.

france24fr.title: Une présentatrice égyptienne condamnée à la peine de mort pour trafic de drogue
france24fr.description: La présentatrice égyptienne Sarah Khalifa, connue pour son émission "Mission difficile" sur la chaîne privée Al-Mehwar, et onze autres personnes ont été condamnées à la peine de mort par le tribunal pénal du Caire, ont rapporté samedi des médias officiels. Elles sont accusées d'avoir fabriqué et trafiqué des stupéfiants.

france24fr.title: Au festival "Visa pour l'image", la guerre au Liban, "la guerre de trop"
france24fr.description: Dans son exposition “la guerre de trop” au festival Visa pour l’image, le photojournaliste libanais Mohammad Yassine revient sur sa couverture de la guerre au Liban pour L’Orient-Le Jour. Depuis le 2 mars 2026, on dénombre plus de 2 000 morts et 7 000 blessés en sept semaines, mais aussi un million de déplacés, soit près d’un habitant sur cinq.

france24fr.title: Premier déplacement des émissaires américains à Kiev : qu'attend l'Ukraine de cette visite ?
france24fr.description: Les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner sont attendus en Ukraine pour la première fois, porteurs selon le président Donald Trump d'une proposition destinée à mettre fin au conflit avec la Russie, après avoir rencontré la veille Vladimir Poutine à Moscou. "Nous souhaitons hâter la fin de la guerre. La paix est nécessaire. Des garanties de sécurité sont nécessaires", a indiqué M. Zelensky, peu avant leur arrivée.

france24fr.title: Émissaires américains à Kiev : "l'Ukraine a besoin de garanties de sécurité" selon Zelensky
france24fr.description: Les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner sont attendus en Ukraine pour la première fois, porteurs selon le président Donald Trump d'une proposition destinée à mettre fin au conflit avec la Russie, après avoir rencontré la veille Vladimir Poutine à Moscou. Ces pourparlers suscitent “des sentiments partagés en Ukraine” raconte Maryna Kumeda, journaliste et écrivaine ukrainienne, invitée de France 24.

france24fr.title: Obsèques de Ratko Mladic en Serbie : l'UE dénonce la "glorification" du criminel de guerre
france24fr.description: Une cérémonie s'est tenue samedi à Belgrade en hommage au criminel de guerre serbe de Bosnie Ratko Mladic, en présence de plusieurs dizaines de militaires, de membres de sa famille et de responsables gouvernementaux, deux jours avant son enterrement dans la capitale serbe.

france24fr.title: Frappes israéliennes à Gaza depuis 2023 : la difficile recherche des disparus
france24fr.description: Dans la bande de Gaza, le calme précaire permet aux secouristes de déblayer des immeubles frappés dès le début de la guerre, en 2023. Ils espèrent retrouver des restes de victimes toujours ensevelies sous les débris. Le bilan dans l'enclave est de 73 000 morts selon un décompte du ministère de la santé palestinien.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Gescheiterte Investorenpläne der Fifa: Fifa-Präsident Infantino tritt 2027 zur Wiederwahl an
nzz.description: Die Fifa wollte einen Teil der kommerziellen Rechte an den Turnieren an private Investoren abgeben. Anfang August hat der Verband das Vorhaben zurückgezogen. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - In Sachsen-Anhalt haben die Wähler die alte Ordnung abgewählt. Aber sie haben keine neue bestellt
nzz.description: Die AfD wird nicht mehr weggehen. Als eindeutige Siegerin ist sie auch nicht mehr politisch zu isolieren. Im Gegenteil: Sie bestimmt so oder so inzwischen mit, unter welchen Bedingungen in dem ostdeutschen Bundesland überhaupt Mehrheiten entstehen können.

nzz.title: Kimi Antonelli schafft in Monza, was sechzig Jahre keinem Italiener mehr gelungen ist – er gewinnt. Und das nach einer denkwürdigen Aufholjagd
nzz.description: Der Italiener triumphiert in seinem Mercedes beim Grossen Preis von Italien – und lässt die Tifosi das Debakel des Nationalrennstalls Ferrari vergessen.

nzz.title: Neuer Vermittlungsversuch der USA: Witkoff und Kushner reisen nach Moskau und erstmals auch nach Kiew
nzz.description: Die amerikanischen Sondergesandten führen Gespräche mit Wladimir Putin und Wolodimir Selenski darüber, wie sie den Krieg beenden können. Die Chancen auf einen diplomatischen Durchbruch sind gering.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Selenski bezeichnet Gespräche mit US-Vermittlern als «sehr substanziell» +++ Der Kreml nennt die Gespräche von Putin und US-Gesandten konstruktiv

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Erstmals erreicht eine private europäische Rakete den Weltraum. Damit sollte sich Europa nicht zufriedengeben
nzz.description: Raketenkrise? Das war einmal. Mit dem Start einer Rakete des deutschen Unternehmens Isar Aerospace macht Europa einen weiteren Schritt in Richtung Souveränität im Weltraum.

nzz.title: Der Kilchberger-Schwinget zeigt, dass dieser traditionsreichen Sportart etwas mehr Exklusivität guttun würde
nzz.description: Samuel Giger gewinnt zum zweiten Mal in Serie das prestigeträchtige Kilchberger. Das Schwingfest, das einst aus Protest ersonnen wurde, bietet eine Vorlage für innovative Wettkampfformate in dieser Sportart.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Sturzflut von Nepal: Zahl der Todesopfer steigt auf knapp 1400 +++ Zwei weitere Überlebende gerettet
nzz.description: Innerhalb weniger Minuten rissen Wasser, Geröll und Eis am 26. August alles in der Grenzregion zwischen China und Nepal mit sich. Mehr als 1000 Personen kamen ums Leben, zahlreiche werden noch vermisst. Die wichtigsten Antworten zur Katastrophe im Himalaja-Tal.

nzz.title: Die USA bombardieren drei iranische Tanker, nachdem Teheran seine Attacken ausgeweitet hat
nzz.description: Zum ersten Mal hat Iran einen amerikanischen Flugzeugträger ins Visier genommen. Während Teheran im Persischen Golf in die Offensive geht, hält es sich bei der Unterstützung des Hizbullah in Libanon zurück.

nzz.title: Demonstranten legen aus Protest gegen die Bootsflüchtlinge den Hafen von Dover lahm
nzz.description: Eine neue Art von Protest sorgt im Südosten Englands für Aufsehen. Hunderte von schwarz gekleideten und vermummten Protestierenden haben am Samstag in einer organisierten Aktion den Fährverkehr zum Erliegen gebracht.

nzz.title: VW-Chef Oliver Blume baut insgesamt 100 000 Stellen ab: Die Börse freut es, doch viele Mitarbeiter müssen weiter bangen
nzz.description: Das amtierende Vorstandsteam des VW-Konzerns hat geschafft, was den Vorgängern oft misslungen ist: die sozialverträgliche Sanierung des verkrusteten Autobauers. Doch die Reise ist noch nicht zu Ende.

nzz.title: Graz droht Zahlungsunfähigkeit: Die Kommunisten müssen einen Ausgabenstopp verhängen
nzz.description: Die Stadt in der Steiermark hat die grösste Pro-Kopf-Verschuldung der österreichischen Städte. Dafür sind nicht nur die regierenden Kommunisten verantwortlich, sie müssen nun aber drastisch sparen.

nzz.title: AfD erreicht höchsten je gemessenen Wert in einem Bundesland – alle Umfragen zur Wahl in Sachsen-Anhalt
nzz.description: Wie schneiden die Parteien vor der Wahl am 6. September in Umfragen ab, welche Koalitionen sind möglich – und was treibt die Menschen in Sachsen-Anhalt um? Hier gibt es die aktuellen Zahlen.

observador.description: Mais de meia centena de pastores do Planalto Mirandês reclamam ao Governo pagamentos atempados devido aos ataques de lobos que têm acontecido nos últimos anos.

observador.title: Os ares de Viseu não mudaram a tendência do clássico
observador.description: A época mudou, mas Viseu trouxe o que já se tinha visto no Jamor: Benfica dominou FC Porto, apesar de ter sido surpreendido a espaços, e reconquistou a Supertaça com naturalidade, com goleada (5-1).

observador.description: A pianista Maria João Pires anunciou o lançamento da primeira edição da "MJP Piano Academy", espaço online dedicado ao ensino de piano. Haverá 'masterclasses' no Centro de Artes de Belgais.

observador.title: A batalha de Londres terminou com o canhão ao alto
observador.description: O Chelsea entrou forte no dérbi e colocou-se a vencer com mais um golaço de Rogers, mas o Arsenal reagiu pelo génio de Havertz e virou o jogo depois do intervalo. Xabi perdeu pela primeira vez (2-1).

observador.title: Milhares de euros, segredos e uma arma: as buscas ao espião
observador.description: Os responsáveis do SIS suspeitavam que Carvalhão Gil trabalhava para os russos há anos. Mas as provas encontradas nas casas do espião ultrapassaram os piores receios. E obrigaram a mudanças profundas.

observador.title: 18h. Alemanha. Projeções dão vitória à AfD nas regionais
observador.description: No entanto, a maioria absoluta ainda é incerta. Volodymyr Zelensky, Jared Kushner e Steve Witkoff fazem um balanço positivo da reunião em Kiev.

observador.title: Von der Leyen chega à Gronelândia com medidas "substanciais"
observador.description: A presidente da Comissão Europeia chegou à Gronelândia levando "um pacote de medidas substancial". Visita pretende reafirmar o compromisso da UE com o território autónomo dinamarquês.

observador.title: BE questiona tempos de espera para psicologia no SNS
observador.description: O Bloco de Esquerda questionou o Governo sobre os tempos de espera para a primeira consulta de psicologia no Serviço Nacional de Saúde. Segundo a bastonária dos psicólogos pode chegar a meio ano.

observador.title: Costa sul da Madeira e Porto Santo sob aviso amarelo
observador.description: O Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera colocou a costa sul da Madeira e a ilha do Porto Santo sob aviso amarelo devido ao tempo quente.

observador.title: 17h. Eleições Alemanha. Participação perto de valor recorde
observador.description: Encerram, por esta hora, as urnas no estado da Saxónia-Anhalt. Perto de 70% dos eleitores compareceram. Possibilidade do partido de extrema-direita AfD conquistar a maioria absoluta.

observador.title: Sondagens dão vitória à AfD com 44% — maioria é improvável
observador.description: Partido de extrema-direita conseguiu obter vitória confortável na Saxónia-Anhalt com 44% das intenções de voto. Ainda assim, projeções não dão maioria absoluta à AfD. CDU em segundo.

observador.title: PS não revela decisão sobre moção de censura
observador.description: O secretário-geral do Partido Socialista recusa assumir qual a decisão que o partido tomará na moção de censura apresentada pelo Chega, mas reafirmou que vai garantir a estabilidade política.

observador.title: Detido jovem suspeito de matar a avó em Mafra
observador.description: Um jovem de 24 anos foi hoje detido por suspeitas de ter matado a avô, de 73 anos, em Milharado, concelho de Mafra.

observador.title: Repatriados 21 migrantes para Marrocos após apedrejamento
observador.description: Vinte e um marroquinos foram repatriados para o seu país de origem após terem atirado pedras contra membros de uma patrulha das Forças Armadas em vigilância na zona da praia El Trampolín.

observador.title: Porta-voz da FIFA confirma recandidatura de Gianni Infantino
observador.description: O ítalo-suíço Gianni Infantino irá recandidatar-se à presidência da FIFA, apesar da crise desencadeada pelo seu plano fracassado, revelou um porta-voz do organismo à France-Presse.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Wählerwanderung bei der Landtagswahl – wer der AfD zum Sieg verhalf
spiegel.description: Sachsen-Anhalt hat gewählt. Bei welchen Wählergruppen konnten die Parteien punkten? Und wer konnte bei wem Stimmen holen? Die Analyse in Grafiken.

spiegel.title: Cyberangriff in Berlin: Hacker veröffentlichen weiteres Datenpaket
spiegel.description: Hacker haben erneut interne Daten ins Netz gestellt, darunter offenbar Zugangsdaten. Der Berliner Senat verschärft seine Sicherheitsmaßnahmen. Für die Bauverwaltung bedeutet das Einschränkungen.

spiegel.title: Robert Pattinson: Schauspieler sieht in seinem Baby den Grund für sehr emsiges Arbeiten
spiegel.description: Der Schauspieler Robert Pattinson hat innerhalb kurzer Zeit vier Filme abgedreht. Wie hat er das geschafft? Dafür lieferte er bei den Filmfestspielen von Venedig eine überraschende Begründung.

spiegel.title: Donald Trumps Friedensplan: Muslimische Staaten verurteilen Israels Umsiedlungsplan für Gazastreifen
spiegel.description: Israels Verteidigungsminister will 250.000 Palästinenser aus dem Gazastreifen vertreiben, die restlichen Bewohner sollen folgen. Mehrere muslimische Staaten warnen vor einem Scheitern des US-Friedensplans.

spiegel.title: Thüringen.Gerecht: Frühere BSW-Mitglieder gründen nach Austritt neue Partei
spiegel.description: »Es gab eine spontane Parteigründung«: Mehrere ehemalige Mitglieder des BSW in Thüringen haben sich zu einer neuen Partei zusammengeschlossen. Die frühere BSW-Landesvorsitzende soll die Führung übernehmen.

spiegel.title: Ronald Koeman Jr. trifft doppelt als Torwart in der Eredivisie
spiegel.description: Gegen Cambuur lag der niederländische Erstligist Telstar 0:2 zurück. Dass das Comeback gelang, lag am Torwart – denn Ronald Koeman Jr. ist nicht nur Sohn des Ex-Nationaltrainers, sondern auch sicher vom Elfmeterpunkt.

spiegel.title: CDU-Desaster in Sachsen-Anhalt: Jetzt wird es richtig chaotisch
spiegel.description: Das Ergebnis halbiert, die Partei in Aufruhr: Die CDU erlebt ein Wahldesaster, wie es selbst die größten Pessimisten nicht für möglich hielten. Die ersten drängen Wahlverlierer Sven Schulze zum Rücktritt.

spiegel.title: Sven Schulze (CDU): Spitzenkandidat reagiert auf CDU-Absturz bei Wahl
spiegel.description: Spitzenkandidat Sven Schulze reagiert bemerkenswert auf den Absturz der CDU – seine Zukunft ist offen, die Stimmung mies. SPIEGEL-Redakteur Peter Maxwill mit Eindrücken von einer Wahlparty, die keine war.

spiegel.title: Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt: Was der haushohe Sieg für Deutschland bedeutet
spiegel.description: Es ist ein Sprung in eine neue Dimension: Die AfD hat in Sachsen-Anhalt haushoch gewonnen. Was das für Deutschland bedeutet.

spiegel.title: Landtagswahl Sachsen-Anhalt: Präsident des Zentralrats der Juden entsetzt über AfD-Wahlergebnis
spiegel.description: Menschen aus der jüdischen Community äußern sich schockiert über den Wahlsieg der AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt. Das Ergebnis übertreffe ihre »schlimmsten Albträume«, sagt die Holocaustüberlebende Charlotte Knobloch.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Reaktionen aus Magdeburg – »Ich stehe da und bin erschüttert«
spiegel.description: Die AfD geht als klarer Sieger aus der Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt hervor. Wie finden das die Menschen? Antworten aus der Landeshauptstadt Magdeburg.

spiegel.title: Frauen-Bundesliga: FC Bayern München stellt Rekord mit 45 Spielen ohne Niederlage auf
spiegel.description: Fast zwei Jahre ist die letzte Liganiederlage des FC Bayern her. Ein Lauf, der sich nun Rekordserie nennen darf: Beim Sieg über Freiburg glänzte vor allem Traumtorschützin Momoko Tanikawa.

spiegel.title: Dänemark: Altkönigin Margrethe II. erneut in Krankenhaus eingeliefert
spiegel.description: Zum dritten Mal in diesem Jahr ist Margrethe II. im Krankenhaus. Die 86-jährige dänische Altkönigin wird wegen Blutergüssen und Dehydrierung behandelt.

spiegel.title: Grönland: Ursula Von der Leyen zu Besuch eingetroffen – Zeichen gegen Donald Trump
spiegel.description: US-Präsident Donald Trump erhebt nach wie vor Ansprüche auf das rohstoffreiche Grönland. Der Besuch der EU-Kommissionspräsidentin soll nun ein Zeichen dagegen setzen – und eine Finanzspritze zusagen.

spiegel.title: Bundesliga: FC Augsburg wird nach Sieg gegen Eintracht Frankfurt Tabellenführer
spiegel.description: Verschlafen aus der Pause, dazu ein Patzer von Noah Atubolu: Mit Eintracht Frankfurts Heimspiel gegen den FC Augsburg geht es im zweiten Durchgang bergab. So sehr, dass die Augsburger gar die Tabellenspitze erobern.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt Wahl: Sven Schulze kommentiert AfD-Sieg – »Das ist Demokratie«
spiegel.description: Ein schwarzer Tag für Sachsen-Anhalt? So möchte der amtierende Ministerpräsident das Wahlergebnis nicht interpretieren. Die Grünen erklären sich ihr solides Resultat auch mit dem Klimawandel. Die Reaktionen.

phys-org.title: Small molecular substitutions reshape energy pathways behind aggregation-induced emission
phys-org.description: Certain chemical substances, broadly called luminogens, have an inherent ability to emit light. Most fluorescent molecules emit light in solution but lose their emission in the solid state, where the molecules aggregate.

phys-org.description: Since scientists can't drill 2,900 km (1,800 miles) to the boundary between Earth's core and deep mantle, they must use information relayed by seismic waves recorded during earthquakes to study this region. phys-org.title: The extinct American 'cheetah' was not a cheetah after all
phys-org.description: With their slender bodies and long front legs, Miracinonyx trumani—often nicknamed the "American cheetah"—was long thought to be a North American analog of the African big cat. But in a new study published in the journal Current Biology, researchers reveal that the extinct cat was more closely related to pumas. Some populations living near the Arctic preyed almost exclusively on fish, challenging the long-held assumption that these "cheetahs" chased fast-running prey, such as pronghorns.

phys-org.title: Extreme pressure turns blue pigment into record-long single-atom copper chains
phys-org.description: As the electronics in our technology keep shrinking, traditional silicon-based chips are approaching their fundamental physical limits. Yet the wires connecting them might be able to shrink beyond conventional dimensions, as scientists have created one of the longest single-atom copper chains to date that could serve as molecular wires.

phys-org.title: How algorithms are making our environments bland
phys-org.description: The Pantone color of the year for 2026 is white. It's called Cloud Dancer, which is described as a "lofty white." This choice reflects a growing trend away from color in our visual world.

phys-org.title: 'Quiet' pulsar suddenly reveals three glitches in 15 years of observations
phys-org.description: Using more than 15 years of observations from the Parkes radio telescope, astronomers detected three rotational glitches in the pulsar PSR J1637−4642—a young neutron star that had shown no signs of glitches since its discovery. The three glitches included one that changed its rotation rate by nearly 3 parts per million. Their paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Aug. 20. It has been accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal Letters.

phys-org.title: Germany's Isar Aerospace launches rocket into orbit from Norway
phys-org.description: Germany's Isar Aerospace launched a rocket into orbit from Norway on Saturday as Europe races to boost its ability to economically send satellites into space independently of the United States.

phys-org.title: Haze emergency grips Malaysian Borneo town
phys-org.description: Acrid smoke hung heavily over the Malaysian town of Serian, seeping into homes and cloaking roadside stalls, as residents navigated an air-quality emergency fueled by transboundary haze from Indonesia's raging fires.

phys-org.title: Breaking through AlphaFold's limits to predict how proteins change shape
phys-org.description: Conformational changes in proteins are vital to their function yet remain challenging for state-of-the-art artificial intelligence, such as AlphaFold3, to predict. Researchers at the Institute for Molecular Science (IMS), and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies, SOKENDAI introduced a repulsive force between predicted structures, allowing AlphaFold3 to sample the multiple conformational states that its default settings rarely capture.

phys-org.title: How much clearcutting can nature sustain? A study determines the ecological limit for boreal forest birds
phys-org.description: A study led by the University of Jyväskylä in Finland evaluated, for the first time, an ecological threshold for the amount of clearcutting in boreal forests. According to the results, maintaining populations of bird species specialized in old-growth forests requires either a forest rotation period of at least 90 years on average or that approximately one-fifth of the forest area be excluded from clearcut management. The study provides a concrete target for the ecologically sustainable use of fo

phys-org.title: FAST finds two mysterious hydrogen clouds with no visible stars
phys-org.description: Astronomers have found two clouds of hydrogen near the Whirlpool galaxy that appear to contain almost no stars. The clouds, discovered with China's FAST radio telescope, each contain roughly 3 million times the mass of the sun in hydrogen but have no detectable optical counterpart. Their properties are outlined in a new paper published in the Astronomy & Astrophysics  journal on Aug. 4.

phys-org.title: Views from a physician and veterinarian: How to improve barriers to pet care when owners are hospitalized
phys-org.description: The human-animal bond is often so strong that pet owners may delay or forgo medical treatment or leave a health care facility against medical advice if they have no one to care for their pet at home. A perspective paper published in the New England Journal of Medicine explains why pet owners may need different approaches to care when hospitalized, according to an Emory University physician and an Ohio State University veterinarian.

phys-org.title: US study tests psilocybin to fight cancer side effects
phys-org.description: Here's a novel idea for countering the painful side effects of chemotherapy: Beforehand, take the hallucinogenic drug found in magic mushrooms.

phys-org.title: A black hole as light as 40 tons can exist inside a star if dark matter helps
phys-org.description: In 1974, Stephen Hawking made a prediction that transformed our understanding of black holes. Black holes, he showed, are not truly black: They slowly lose energy through a quantum process now known as Hawking radiation. The lighter the black hole, the faster it evaporates.

phys-org.title: Tree species diversity protects forests from climate extremes, study finds
phys-org.description: New research has found that tree species diversity can play a crucial role in protecting forests from the growing threat of extreme climate events. The study analyzed data from 88,116 separate forest plots across the United States to investigate the impact of "compound climate extremes," when events such as drought and extreme heat occur at the same time.

phys-org.title: Scientists discover how narwhals grow nature's only straight tusk
phys-org.description: Narwhals have nature's only straight tusk, a single tooth up to three meters (10 feet) long, so strange they were sold as magical unicorn horns during the Middle Ages.

phys-org.title: Some disagreement makes groups more trustworthy, mathematical framework finds
phys-org.description: When humans are making decisions, they are known not to rely solely on their own considerations and the evidence available to them. Past behavioral science and psychology studies have shown that people are often also influenced by the choices and opinions of others.

phys-org.title: Lakes aren't just storing water—they're changing the carbon cycle
phys-org.description: Lakes may look like picturesque stopping points along a river or stream, but they can have a big influence on what happens to carbon as it moves through a landscape. New research suggests that the more lake-rich a network of streams is, the more carbon is released into the atmosphere rather than carried downstream.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

proj-syn.title: How Developing Countries Can Do More With Less
proj-syn.description: Evaluation frameworks for development projects have long been influenced by donor priorities. proj-syn.title: America’s Naval Disaster
proj-syn.description: Plagued by exorbitant costs and chronic delays, American shipbuilders cannot produce enough vessels to keep pace with China. US President Donald Trump’s push to rebuild the industry does little to address its underlying problems and threatens to squander hundreds of billions of dollars.

proj-syn.title: America’s Un-American AI Companies
proj-syn.description: The United States can prevail in the AI race against China by leaning into the strengths of an open society: democratic oversight, the rule of law, robust competition, and open public debate. But that won’t happen as long as American AI companies aggressively lobby against accountability and cozy up to the state.

proj-syn.title: The Golden Bridge to Monetary Multipolarity
proj-syn.description: Gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world’s top reserve asset because it offers a solution to the challenges of a rogue America. But its renewed relevance also reflects how rapid technological diffusion and increasing dispersion of economic power are creating a more diversified international monetary system.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Natural Disasters Must Not Become Financial Crises
proj-syn.description: The dangerous flooding in Nepal and Tibet has demonstrated, once again, the need for prearranged disaster-risk financing to prepare for the economic chain reactions triggered by natural disasters. Asia’s policymakers must act now to help cash-strapped Nepal and strengthen other countries’ resilience before the next crisis hits.

proj-syn.title: Is AI Crowding Out Other Investment?
proj-syn.description: The AI investment boom has unleashed a wave of demand for capital just as savings are declining and interest rates remain high. As competition for financing intensifies, rising borrowing costs could squeeze non-AI firms looking to finance new factories, equipment, and projects.

proj-syn.title: India’s Resilience Depends on Diversified Trade
proj-syn.description: India has signed a flurry of trade deals since Donald Trump’s return to the White House in an attempt to ensure that no single bilateral rupture will cause catastrophic harm. It should continue to expand its trade ties, while being wary of any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action vis-à-vis third countries.

proj-syn.title: Whipsaw Trade Policy Is Depressing Foreign Direct Investment
proj-syn.description: If a country opts for higher trade restrictions to promote its perceived domestic interests, a predictable policy is far superior to a volatile one. As new research shows, uncertainty causes unnecessary and large collateral damage to FDI inflows.

proj-syn.title: Why the Far Right’s War on Modern Architecture Matters
proj-syn.description: The Alternative for Germany’s fixation on architecture is more revealing than it may seem. Cultural policy is not only one area where the party can actually change conditions on the ground at the state level; it is also intimately tied to far-right forces’ exclusionary political agenda.

proj-syn.title: How Will the US-Iran War End?
proj-syn.description: The latest US effort to subdue Iran—an "economic D-Day" intended to cut off the Islamic Republic from the world economy—can’t succeed without the support of the country’s biggest trade partner. The only stable solution to the impasse in the Gulf is one that involves China and increases economic integration in the region.

proj-syn.title: Germany’s Political Firewall Is Crumbling
proj-syn.description: The upcoming election in Saxony-Anhalt could give the far-right Alternative für Deutschland control of a state government for the first time in Germany’s postwar history. Its rise offers a crucial lesson for democracies elsewhere: closing ranks against extremist parties is no substitute for effective governance.

proj-syn.title: The Swimmable City Test
proj-syn.description: In committing to provide a safe swimmable place within 15 minutes of every home by 2035, London Mayor Sadiq Khan has set a measurable, time-bound goal that cannot be met through a single program or line item on the budget. Instead, it requires a public mission capable of mobilizing all ministries and shaping markets.

proj-syn.title: The Tale of Economics
proj-syn.description: A new book tells the story of the economics discipline and its original purpose with a degree of verve and imaginativeness that puts dreary mainstream economists to shame. In the process, it gets at fundamental truths that major schools within the discipline have managed to obscure.

proj-syn.title: AI’s Market Path Will Get Bumpier
proj-syn.description: By enhancing the input that goes into so much of what we do—intelligence—AI’s potential to drive higher economic growth is enormous. But with fears of the technology's unintended consequences affecting the pace and depth of adoption, the promise of long-term gains must be set against more immediate risks.

proj-syn.title: American Götterdämmerung
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump and his Treasury secretary’s latest desperate threats confirm how much American power has waned on their watch. Far from compelling others to join their efforts to isolate Iran, they are hastening the transition to a post-American world order.

proj-syn.title: Hard Lessons for Europe From the Ceuta Crisis
proj-syn.description: European Union leaders should have received several messages during the recent surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In particular, cohesion without trust is fragile; dependence without limits leads to vulnerability; and selective enforcement of international law risks eroding a pillar of Europe’s strategic identity.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Silent Majority for International Cooperation
proj-syn.description: The hollowing out of global institutions has resulted in a rapid loss of credibility for the international rule of law. But a majority of people worldwide still recognize the value of multilateralism, which countries can preserve in the absence of superpower consent by finding better ways to cooperate.

proj-syn.title: Building Canada’s Post-American Economy
proj-syn.description: Canada’s dependence on the US market has become a strategic liability, leaving it vulnerable to President Donald Trump’s bullying. Reducing that dependence will require building industries that can compete globally while removing the structural barriers that prevent innovative Canadian firms from scaling.

crunchbase.title: Global Venture Funding Jumps 122% In August As Streak Of Billion-Dollar Deals Continues
crunchbase.description: Venture investors poured $42 billion into just over 1,500 startups worldwide in August, Crunchbase data shows, down 25% from July’s $56 billion but still up a significant 122% compared to last August, which is typically a slower month for startup investment.

crunchbase.title: Former Apple Engineers’ Physical AI Startup Lyte Raises $165M At $1.6B Valuation
crunchbase.description: Lyte, a physical AI startup building sensing and perception technology for robots, has raised a Maverick Silicon-led $165 million Series C funding at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation.

crunchbase.title: The IPO Window Is Closing. Here Are 8 Startups To Watch.
crunchbase.description: In the first half of this year, 58 venture-backed companies joined the public listings at $1 billion or above, per Crunchbase data. With the year’s end now in sight, a small window remains for other startups to launch 2026 IPOs, so we took a look at notable venture-backed startups that Crunchbase’s predictive intelligence suggests are potential IPO candidates within the next six months.

crunchbase.title: WhatsApp Remittance Startup Félix Secures $200M Series C Led By A16z, General Catalyst
crunchbase.description: Félix, a Miami-based AI-powered WhatsApp remittance platform for Latino immigrants, announced on Tuesday that it has secured $200 million in Series C funding co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and General Catalyst.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Proptech Funding Holds Up, But Investors Are Placing Different Bets
crunchbase.description: Real estate tech startup investors are being more selective about their bets and putting more money into companies using AI and other technology to make construction, property operations and real estate transactions faster and less expensive.

crunchbase.title: Biotech Startup Investment Held Steady Even As AI Funding Surged
crunchbase.description: While the AI boom has disrupted funding patterns across the startup sphere, biotech has remained a rare steady sector for investment. For the past few years, global funding to biotech startups has hovered between $36 billion and $40 billion. Per Crunchbase data, 2026 is on track to stay close to that range.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Tools And Assistants Lead Sparser Lineup Of Megadeals
crunchbase.description: Most of this week’s largest funding recipients were AI-focused startups, with Instinct, a developer of AI assistants, pulling in the biggest round.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Space Tech Startup Funding Orbits New Highs
crunchbase.description: So far this year, a record $20.3 billion in global seed- through growth-stage funding has gone to companies in space- and satellite-related sectors, per Crunchbase data. That’s already by far the highest annual tally on record, and we’ve still got four months left in 2026.
